description.p: Sealwax is a fast, minimal email client, quick to drive from the keyboard and careful with every message: no script in a message ever runs, and nothing from the internet loads until you allow it.

ul.li: Accounts without server settings: type your address and Sealwax finds the servers; Sign in with Microsoft for Outlook.com and Microsoft 365, app passwords for others
IMAP with push and an offline copy of your mail, and POP3 into local folders
Whole conversations, safe HTML, attachments that open safely and link warnings
Archive, delete, move, star and mark many messages at once, with Undo, also offline
Folders, and rules in Sieve, the standard mail-filter language, made in a dialog
A rich-text composer, drafts kept on the server and an outbox with Undo send
Search with from:, to:, subject:, has:attachment and more, with suggestions as you type
Unsubscribe in one click, group mail by sender or domain, and pin the senders you mustn't miss
One-key shortcuts, a command palette and your own keys
Passwords only in your keyring, no telemetry, and logs without mail content

description.p: Sealwax follows the system's light or dark style. On Omarchy it also follows the live theme and Hyprland's rounded corners.
Help: the user guide is at pixdevs.com/guides/sealwax, and support answers at support@pixdevs.com. Contact Support… in Sealwax's main menu gives you the address and the details that help.

description.p: The unread count Sealwax shares with bars and scripts now takes in the folders under your Inboxes and your own folders, leaving out Sent, Drafts, Archive, Junk and Trash. In Omarchy's bar, a click on Sealwax's icon lists the folders with unread mail, and a click on one opens Sealwax there.

Files dragged from a file manager onto the composer are attached again on Hyprland, which offers such a drop only as a move. Before, the composer turned the drop down, and over the message text the file went in as its address. The file is always copied, never moved.

Messages can be signed and encrypted with your own GnuPG keyring and gpg-agent, as PGP/MIME. Encrypting needs a key for every recipient and never falls back to plain text, and a draft marked Encrypt stays on your computer.

Two fixes to PGP signature checking: a signature is called checked only when your keyring vouches for the sender's own address on the key, and text written around a clear-signed message is no longer shown as signed.

PGP mail is decrypted with your own GnuPG keyring and gpg-agent, and its signatures are checked: a signature is called checked only when your keyring vouches for the sender's key. The decrypted text is never saved or searched.

Attached emails, such as a forwarded message or the original inside an Italian certified email (PEC), open in the reader with a way back. A message can be handed to a program of your own with Open With, set up in config.toml.

A security release. Sealwax now sends mail with lettre 0.11.24 instead of its own patched copy. A line of only spaces in a server's list of features could crash an account's background work and take the account offline for a while; that no longer happens.
An answer from the server after a sent message that can only belong to another command now leaves the send uncertain, so Sealwax asks you to check your Sent folder.

Conversations as one row in the message list: choose Group by Conversation in the new Group by menu at the end of the filter chips. Each row shows the newest message, how many messages the conversation has and whether any is unread, and selecting it shows the whole conversation.
Archive, Delete and Mark as Read act on the conversation's messages in the folder shown, and say so.

Mail sends through IONOS again: its server refuses a second request for its features, which left every message waiting in the outbox. Sealwax now carries on with the features the server named the first time.

Signatures with your photo or logo, contact details and social profiles, made in a form and readable in light and dark mail, or from your own HTML file. Go to any folder from the keyboard, forward messages as attachments and keep searches in the sidebar.
While Sealwax runs it shares your unread count, so a bar widget or a script can show it.

Updated libraries: rusqlite 0.43 and ammonia 4.1.9, which clear published advisories that did not reach Sealwax. SQLite 3.45.3 or later is now needed. Software centres find Sealwax by more search words, and its website link is now its product page.

After Empty Trash, Delete in the Trash or Send, the toast's Undo now goes when its seven seconds are up. A toast the pointer rested on used to keep showing an Undo that could no longer undo. If Undo had the keyboard focus, the focus returns to the message list.

Empty Trash: an account's Trash folder has Empty Trash on its sidebar menu, which deletes the folder's messages for good, on the server too, including older mail Sealwax never downloaded. Undo in the toast stands for the usual seven seconds.

Help, also without a GitHub account: the main menu's Help submenu has User Guide, which opens the online guide, Contact Support…, which shows the support address with the details that help and can start the message, Report an Issue and About Sealwax. The setup assistant offers the same help when an account can't be added.

The message list can be shown on its own, without the reading pane: Toggle Reading Pane in the main menu makes a message open in the list's place, in a window of any width. The keyboard stays in the list when the window changes width, and one folder a mail server won't report on no longer hides an account's other folders.

Sealwax as a Flatpak, for Linux systems other than Omarchy, from Sealwax's own Flatpak repository, with updates through Flatpak. Software centres can now describe Sealwax, and a network monitor that first says there is no network no longer makes every account reconnect at start.
A security update: a mail server can no longer keep Sealwax busy with one long reply.
Folders with a backslash or a quote in their name sync.
The message list keeps its place when rows change under the selection.
